summary: Mostly consistent, but R5 has no test that names it (so TEST-001 cannot pass) and R2's second acceptance line is a visual judgement no automated test can prove.

conflicts.why: The design's only test component covers R1, R2, R3, R4 and A1, and docs/expand-collapse.md is listed separately with R5 and no test, so no automated test names R5 and TEST-001 ('every requirement is proven by at least one test that names it') fails as the plan stands. A doc-assertion test in the new test file would fix it without changing any requirement.
conflicts.evidence: TEST-001: 'Every requirement is proven by at least one test that names it.' Design components: {"name": "MobileChevronPlacementTests", ... "requirements": ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "A1"]} and {"name": "ExpandCollapseDocs", "path": "docs/expand-collapse.md", "requirements": ["R5"]}. R5: 'The documentation that describes the mobile chevron as a top-of-card row is updated to describe it as a bottom-of-card row.'

conflicts.why: R2's second acceptance line is a visual judgement ('reads visually as the last row') that no automated test can prove; the design's substitute is a CSS contract test that only asserts the presence of border-top/margin-top in the text of the module.css file (CSS values cannot be read through computed styles because CSS is mapped to identity-obj-proxy), so QA could never accept that line on evidence. The acceptance line needs rewording to something provable (e.g. the row has border-top/margin-top and its top border is adjacent to the last data row), or the requirement must say how it is accepted.
conflicts.evidence: R2 acceptance: 'The chevron row reads visually as the last row of the card, separated from the last data row above it.' Design A1: 'A CSS contract test asserts the .mobileExpandRow block has border-top and margin-top and no border-bottom or margin-bottom, and keeps justify-content: flex-start and rem spacing.' Project note: 'moduleNameMapper maps CSS to identity-obj-proxy, so CSS values cannot be asserted through computed styles - a CSS contract test must read the module.css file'.
